detail.longDescription: arXiv:2611.33365v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Geofeeds allow IP address resource owners to self-publish the geolocation of their prefixes, and adoption has grown substantially: as of November 2026, more than 5,000 geofeeds cover 1.6M prefixes. We measure geofeed errors, inconsistencies, and flaws by collecting geofeed references from the WHOIS of all five RIRs weekly over three months and downloading every referenced geofeed. The share of WHOIS objects complying with RFC 9632, which specifies how inetnum objects reference geofeeds, drops from 90% to 61%, driven by a single operator's objects with multiple geofeed references. Each week, 12-20% of geofeed URLs cannot be downloaded, and one in five downloaded geofeeds violates RFC 8805, which defines the geofeed CSV format. Moreover, 17% of geofeeds list IPv4 prefixes whose WHOIS object references a different geofeed. Finally, 281k prefixes appear in more than one geofeed, 3.8k of them with conflicting locations, and for 26% of these conflicts no geofeed is authoritative. We publish our results on a public dashboard, which one large CDN has already used to fix its geofeeds.
